newsitem.title: UK: Dlr closes near six-week highs vs mark in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr closes near six-week highs vs mark in Europe.

text.p: The dollar reached six-week highs against the mark in European trading, buoyed by Swiss franc weakness and gaining extra support from much stronger than expected U.S. economic data, analysts said.
The Swiss currency fell to a 23-month low against the dollar at 1.3145 Swiss francs and also weakened to its lowest level since February 1995 against the mark at 85.15 centimes.

The perception that continued economic weakness in Switzerland will keep Swiss interest rates low undermined the franc, combined with a prevailing strategy of selling the franc as a funding currency for higher yielding units, traders said.

A much stronger than expected reading of the National Association of Purchasing Mangement (NAPM) index also helped underpin the dollar. The NAPM stood at 52.7 in November, up from 50.2 in October and against 50.8 forecast.
However, a drop in the key prices component of the index to 45.9 from 47.1 offset some of the inflationary implications of the report, analysts said.

"The data is still in line with moderate non-inflationary growth, but recent statistics have hinted at some acceleration in (economic) activity," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist Europe at Bank of America in London.
The dollar was at 1.5421/31 marks at 1600 GMT, just off a high at 1.5437 and up from 1.5376/83 in late Europe on Friday.
Construction spending, also released on Monday, rose by a robust 1.8 percent in October, the biggest rise in seven months.

"There is nothing to upset the Fed at this stage, but given the tightness of the labour market, more of the same could yet force the central bank's hand early next year," said Hawkins. Against the yen, the dollar recouped early losses made in the wake of comments by Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita. Dollar/yen stood at 113.69/76 compared with 113.82/92 at the previous European close.

The yen was buoyed by Matsushita's comment that the gradual economic recovery in Japan was becoming more solid, traders said. But buying by U.S. names lifted dollar/yen off its lows. The 114 yen level, however, remains a solid barrier amid talk of large sell orders there, traders said.
Key levels to watch out for on the dollar now are the October 17 high at 1.5454 marks and 1.3187 Swiss francs, the January 1994 high, analysts said.
"The dollar sliced through 1.30 (Swiss francs) easily, and with more Swissie weakness expected, dollar/mark should strengthen more as well," said a senior trader at a German bank.
German corporate selling interest at 1.5450 marks might cap the mark for now though, the trader said.
Speculation about a near-term cut in German interest rates is likely to resurface ahead of Thursday's Bundesbank coucil meeting as lots of German data will hit the markets this week.
The figures include third quarter GDP on Wednesday, November jobless data on Thursday and October industrial production some time this week.
Also dollar-supportive were recent comments by French President Jacques Chirac, Finance Minister Jean Arthuis and Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet, traders said.

They all lent their support to continuing the franc fort policy. Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, meanwhile, said investors might choose to switch to dollar denominated assets at the onset of European monetary union (EMU).

EMU optimism was recharged by comments by Juergen Stark, state secretary at the German Finance Ministry, who said he expected the main elements of the stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline in single-currency Europe to be agreed by the December 13 EU summit in Dublin.
The lira rose close to 2 1/2 year highs at 986.50 per mark.
-- Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
